scope: L1 mechanical only; no product fixes; no exploit PoC

findings.title: Same github.io origin as WeeklySocialMediaIdea PAT-in-localStorage (F-web-gist-pat-localstorage class)
findings.claim: This project page shares the scheme/host/port origin https://chinchiang.github.io with WeeklySocialMediaIdea. Sibling live JS stores a GitHub token under localStorage key wsmi-gh-token and sends Authorization: Bearer to api.github.com for gist sync. This repo's own HTML/JS does not contain PAT/gist/api.github.com code, but any script executing on this origin (including XSS via this site's innerHTML sinks) can read sibling keys. This site also writes localStorage key lang.

severity.rationale: Classic github.io project-page origin sharing. A gist-scoped PAT in localStorage is readable by every project under the same user Pages host. Combined with this site's 15 innerHTML assignments and absent CSP, an XSS in WeekReportfromClaude is a trampoline to the sibling token. Token is not hardcoded in either landing HTML; risk is runtime storage on a shared origin.

evidence: rg on *.html/*.js in this repo: 0 matches for github_pat_|ghp_|ghpat_|api.github.com|Authorization|Bearer
sibling index CSP connect-src https://api.github.com; UI button sync-cfg title 同步設定（設定/更換/移除 Token）

sibling assets/app.js: LS_TOKEN='wsmi-gh-token'; token(){return localStorage.getItem(LS_TOKEN)||''}; headers Authorization Bearer + token(); fetch('https://api.github.com'+path); gist create/search/PATCH; setupToken prompt for classic PAT with gist scope
findings.reachability: Internet-facing. Requires (a) a user who previously stored a PAT on the sibling page in the same browser profile, and (b) attacker JS on this origin (XSS, malicious commit to this public Pages site, or another same-origin project). No PAT string is present in this repo tree.
findings.blast_radius: Disclosure of a GitHub classic PAT with gist scope from the visitor's browser; gist read/write as that user; possible token reuse if the user over-scoped the PAT. Does not by itself grant this repo's GitHub write access.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not store PATs in localStorage on github.io project pages. Move either site to a unique origin (user/org custom domain, or separate GitHub user/org Pages). Add a strict CSP on this site (default-src 'self'; no script-src unsafe-inline once scripts are extracted). Treat any XSS on this origin as credential theft of sibling keys.
findings.promotion: Promote to L2: confirm XSS reachability from committed JSON through innerHTML/href sinks; confirm sibling key names still live; do not emit a steal PoC.
findings.human_triage: Confirm whether any operator actually pastes a PAT into WeeklySocialMediaIdea on browsers that also open this weekly report. If yes, rotate those tokens. Decide whether github.io shared origin is acceptable for this pair of public sites.

findings.title: This repo uses localStorage only for UI language; no PAT/gist/auto-sync in tree
findings.claim: Mechanical search of all HTML/JS in this repo found localStorage getItem/setItem solely for key lang. sessionStorage: none. No ghpat_/ghp_/github_pat_ literals. No api.github.com, gist sync, Authorization, or Bearer in HTML/JS. m07 pages do not touch Web Storage.

severity.rationale: Own stored data is a language preference, not a secret. Severity is informational except as it participates in shared-origin key collision/read (see L1-F01). Key name lang is generic and could be overwritten by any same-origin page.

findings.reachability: Any same-origin script can read or overwrite lang. Impact is UI language flip, not credential theft from this key.
findings.blast_radius: Preference integrity only for this key.
findings.proposed_fix: Optional: namespace the key (e.g. wrfc-lang) to avoid sibling collisions. Not a substitute for L1-F01 origin isolation.
findings.promotion: Do not promote unless L2 is already reviewing origin sharing.
findings.human_triage: Record as clean for PAT-in-this-repo. Do not treat absence of token strings as absence of origin risk.

findings.title: Live Pages responses lack CSP and other browser isolation headers
findings.claim: Live HTML/JSON responses include access-control-allow-origin: * and GitHub/Fastly cache headers, but no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or Strict-Transport-Security on the captured HTTPS 200. HTML has no CSP meta. http:// redirects 301 to https://. GitHub API reports https_enforced=true. m07 pages load Google Fonts without a CSP allowlist.

severity.rationale: Missing CSP is the control that would have contained XSS and blocked connect-src to api.github.com from this origin. ACAO * is GitHub Pages default and makes JSON readable cross-origin (data is already public). HSTS may still be set at the github.io apex on other paths; it was not present on these 200 responses.

evidence: same header set on reports/index.json, m07/, m07/archive.html
m07 index.html: robots noindex + fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com stylesheets
gh api pages: https_enforced=true, source main /
findings.reachability: Every visitor of the public site. Header absence is unconditional.
findings.blast_radius: No containment if XSS or third-party script/CSS runs; JSON is fetchable from any origin via ACAO *.
findings.proposed_fix: GitHub Pages cannot set most security headers on project pages without a custom domain + extra config. Mitigate in HTML: CSP meta (will break inline scripts unless hashes/nonces are added), X-Content-Type-Options cannot be set from HTML. Consider custom domain with header controls, or move scripts out of inline and add CSP. Self-host fonts.
findings.promotion: L2 should assess whether a CSP-with-hashes is feasible for the three inline-script pages and whether Google Fonts CSS is an acceptable third party.
findings.human_triage: Accept as GitHub Pages platform limitation vs. treat as a reason to stop putting privileged-adjacent UI on this origin (L1-F01).

findings.title: innerHTML-heavy renderers consume repo JSON; href URLs are HTML-escaped but not protocol-allowlisted
findings.location: index.html (11 assigns), modules/07-ai-model-watch/index.html (2), archive.html (2); href sinks at index.html:849, m07 index.html:284,311
findings.claim: Three public HTML files assign innerHTML 15 times. Report fields generally pass through esc() (textContent or [&<>"] replace). Gaps: (1) source URLs are interpolated into href after HTML-escape only — javascript: and data: survive; (2) loadFail(id) interpolates id unescaped if fetch fails; (3) week-list title fallback uses raw r.id when esc(title) is empty; (4) siteLogo and indexFail inject static HTML by design; (5) fetch(`reports/${id}.json`) has no YYYY-Www allowlist. eval/document.write/insertAdjacentHTML/outerHTML count is 0.

severity.rationale: Not reflected XSS from the URL hash alone: loadIndex only loadReport()s an id that exists in reports/index.json. Stored XSS requires a malicious or compromised reports/*.json or m07 data/*.json commit (public repo, routine-written). Combined with L1-F01, that is a PAT-theft path, not just defacement.

evidence: m07 archive.html:110 same esc; highlight via RegExp on already-escaped text
findings.reachability: Attacker needs write to committed JSON (direct push, accepted PR, or compromised routine). Hash-only visitors cannot inject id unless it already exists in the index.
findings.blast_radius: Arbitrary JS in visitor browsers on https://chinchiang.github.io — including localStorage of all project pages (L1-F01).
findings.proposed_fix: Allowlist http/https for href; escape id everywhere; never use raw r.id in innerHTML; constrain fetch id to /^\d{4}-W\d{2}$/; prefer textContent/DOM APIs over innerHTML for untrusted JSON.
findings.promotion: Promote to L2 for sink-by-sink reachability (javascript: URL, empty-title id, topic key in nav href). No PoC in L1.
findings.human_triage: Review who can push reports/*.json (humans vs Claude Routine). Treat JSON authors as HTML authors.

findings.title: Sole in-repo workflow uses mutable action tags; persist-credentials left at default; no custom secrets
findings.claim: Only in-repo workflow is 模組 07 資料稽核. permissions.contents: read at workflow level. Triggers: push (all branches, path-filtered), pull_request (path-filtered), workflow_dispatch. Steps: actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-python@v5 (tag, not commit SHA). persist-credentials not set (checkout default true). Run step is a static python3 scripts/generate_week.py --validate-only with no ${{ github.event.* }} interpolation. No secrets.* or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY references. No pull_request_target. Pages deploy is not this workflow — GitHub dynamic pages-build-deployment from branch main. generate_week.py uses only stdlib.

severity.rationale: Unpinned tags are supply-chain mutability. Default persist-credentials leaves GITHUB_TOKEN on disk for later steps; here later steps are local Python with contents:read only and no network client. No secrets-on-PR issue. Event injection into shell not observed.

evidence: concurrency group m07-validate-${{ github.ref }} only github.ref interpolation
generate_week.py imports: argparse, json, sys, datetime, pathlib only
findings.reachability: Any push/PR touching modules/07-ai-model-watch/** runs on GitHub-hosted runners. Fork PRs get the restricted GITHUB_TOKEN, not custom secrets (none configured in YAML).
findings.blast_radius: Compromise of checkout@v4 or setup-python@v5 tags could run on this repo's CI with contents:read. Cannot deploy Pages from this workflow. Token persist is low impact given permission pin.
findings.proposed_fix: Pin actions to full commit SHAs with version comments. Set persist-credentials: false. Keep contents: read. Continue to avoid secrets and pull_request_target.
findings.promotion: L2 optional: inspect GitHub-managed pages-build-deployment permissions and environment protection. In-repo workflow is otherwise low risk.
findings.human_triage: Confirm no repo/org Actions secrets exist that YAML does not reference. Confirm Pages remains branch-deploy from main, not Actions.

findings.title: gitleaks tree+history: one generic-api-key hit is a CVE id false positive
findings.claim: gitleaks detect on working tree and on 49-commit git history each reported 1 finding: RuleID generic-api-key, Secret 'CVE-2026-18577.', Match 'authentication bypass, CVE-2026-18577. '. No GitHub PAT, AWS, Slack, or PEM findings.

severity.rationale: The matched string is a CVE identifier in a public weekly report, not a credential.

evidence: gitleaks detect (history): same finding in commit aa3a6bd596d1190c40d727f69d6e58cbf240bc3d
49 commits scanned, ~1.25 MB history, ~708 KB tree
findings.proposed_fix: Optional gitleaks allowlist for CVE-\d{4}-\d+ if noise matters. No rotation.
findings.human_triage: Mark false positive. No token rotation.

findings.title: No package ecosystem for OSV/npm; Python tool is stdlib-only
findings.location: repository root (no package.json / lockfiles / requirements.txt / pyproject.toml)
findings.claim: osv-scanner v2.0.2 recursive scan: 'No package sources found'. No npm/yarn/pnpm/composer/go/cargo/gem manifests. generate_week.py imports only the Python standard library. No dependency CVEs to file.

severity.rationale: Absence of third-party application dependencies. Residual supply chain is GitHub Actions tags (L1-F05) and Google Fonts CSS (L1-F03).

evidence: osv-scanner --format json -r /workspace -> No package sources found
glob package.json, requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, go.mod, Cargo.toml, Gemfile, composer.json: 0
findings.proposed_fix: None. If npm is added later, re-run OSV.
findings.human_triage: Record clean. Do not confuse Actions/font third parties with application deps.

findings.title: Pages source is main (legacy branch deploy), currently identical to default HEAD
findings.location: GitHub Pages settings (API) vs default branch claude/security-weekly-report-site-joles7
findings.claim: Repo default branch is claude/security-weekly-report-site-joles7 (origin/HEAD). Pages source is main, path /. At scan time origin/main == default HEAD == a105139. README still tells operators to select branch main. Drift between default and Pages source is a future deploy/integrity risk, not an active mismatch.

severity.rationale: No current content skew. Split-brain remains a process footgun if default keeps moving and main does not, or vice versa.

evidence: gh api pages source.branch=main source.path=/ build_type=legacy
git rev-parse HEAD and origin/main both a1051392e0b595eeb697c212eb55851eeeacbdb8
findings.reachability: Operators pushing only to default would not update the live site if main diverges.
findings.blast_radius: Stale public content or surprise publish from main, not a vulnerability by itself.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep default and Pages source the same branch, or document that Pages tracks main only.
findings.human_triage: Confirm this dual-branch setup is intentional.
